title: Where These 4 Sector ETFs Stand Heading Into Year-End
author: James Brumley
description: As 2026 winds down, the article analyzes four key sector ETFs heading into 2027. Technology stocks have pulled back 14% from October highs after AI companies missed earnings, but the sector remains reasonably valued. Financial stocks are mixed, with insurance outperforming while banks struggle amid tepid loan demand. Energy stocks surged 40% YTD on oil prices but face headwinds as crude may have peaked around $90/barrel. Healthcare stocks are up 21% but appear slightly overvalued at current levels.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recent 14% pullback from October highs is viewed as a healthy reset to more reasonable valuations. Forward P/E of just above 20 is considered reasonable, and AI technology still has practical value despite near-term volatility.
Mixed performance with insurance stocks performing well due to higher interest rates, while banks struggle with tepid loan demand. Selective approach recommended rather than broad sector investment.

While up 40% YTD, the sector faces headwinds in 2027 as oil prices near $90/barrel resistance level. EIA predicts crude will average around $80 in 2027, and alternatives to oil are expanding, limiting upside potential.

Despite 21% YTD gains, the ETF is slightly overvalued with forward P/E above 22 and overbought technical conditions. Market may be pricing in results unlikely to materialize until 2028, suggesting a pullback is warranted.

title: Why Is State Street (STT) Up 3.6% Since Last Earnings Report?
author: Na
description: State Street Corporation reported Q3 2026 earnings of $3.69 per share, beating the consensus estimate of $3.65, with net income up 28.4% year-over-year. AUC/A and AUM reached record levels of $59.17 trillion and $6.31 trillion respectively. However, total revenues of $4 billion missed the consensus estimate of $4.04 billion. The company raised its 2026 NII guidance to the upper end of 15-16% range but also increased expense guidance to 8-8.5%. State Street holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with an aggregate VGM Score of F.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed results with earnings beat and record AUM levels offset by revenue miss and rising expenses. Positive guidance revisions for NII but increased expense outlook. Stock rated Hold (Rank #3) with poor growth and momentum scores (F ratings), suggesting in-line returns expected in coming months.

title: Is Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight Health Care ETF (RSPH) a Strong ETF Right Now?
author: Zacks.Com
description: RSPH, an equal-weight healthcare ETF managed by Invesco, has delivered strong year-to-date returns of 30.11% and 12-month returns of 36.18% as of November 11, 2026. With $1.04 billion in assets and a 0.40% expense ratio, it provides diversified exposure to 64 healthcare holdings. However, investors seeking lower-cost alternatives may consider VHT (0.09% expense ratio) or XLV (0.08% expense ratio), which track traditional market-cap weighted healthcare indexes.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: RSPH has delivered strong performance with 30.11% YTD and 36.18% 12-month returns, manages $1.04 billion in assets, and offers competitive 0.40% expense ratio with effective diversification across 64 holdings.
VHT offers a significantly lower expense ratio of 0.09% and manages $21.15 billion in assets, making it an attractive lower-cost alternative for healthcare exposure.
XLV provides the lowest expense ratio at 0.08% and manages the largest asset base at $50.74 billion, positioning it as a cost-efficient option for healthcare sector investment.

title: Can State Street Sustain Its Strong Revenue Growth Trajectory?
author: Na
description: State Street Corporation reported 15% revenue growth to $11.85 billion in the first nine months of 2026, driven by 18.6% growth in net interest income and 14.4% increase in fee revenues. Record assets under custody/administration ($59.2 trillion) and assets under management ($6.3 trillion) support continued expansion. The company maintains positive operating leverage and expects NII growth of 15-16% for full-year 2026, with medium-term projections of low- to mid-single-digit growth.

title: Should You Invest in the iShares U.S. Financial Services ETF (IYG)?
author: Na
description: The iShares U.S. Financial Services ETF (IYG) is a passively managed fund tracking the Dow Jones U.S. Financial Services Index with $2.27 billion in assets. It offers a 0.37% expense ratio and 1.08% dividend yield, with top holdings including Berkshire Hathaway (13.64%), JPMorgan Chase, and Visa. Year-to-date performance is 4.27%, with a beta of 0.97 and standard deviation of 17.19%, making it a high-risk option. The fund holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy).
